The Film

In 1943, a Cincinnati record-shop owner named Syd Nathan started a label in a building on Brewster Avenue where songs could be written, recorded, pressed and shipped without leaving the premises. He called it King. At a time when the industry and the country were divided by race and genre, King recorded hillbilly music and rhythm and blues in the same room, with the same house band, and sold both to anyone who would buy them.

The results rewrote the sound of the century: James Brown's first records, Hank Ballard's original "The Twist," Wynonie Harris's "Good Rockin' Tonight," the Stanley Brothers' bluegrass. King of Them All tells that story through rare archival footage, newly colorized film and hand-drawn animation, and through the people who were there and the musicians who still carry its sound.

Vince Gill
Country Music Hall of Fame member and GRAMMY® winner, on the country side of the King catalog.
Christian McBride
Jazz bassist, composer and GRAMMY® winner, on the rhythm sections that came out of King.
Seymour Stein
Co-founder of Sire Records. Started his career at King as a teenager, working for Syd Nathan.

With Tammy Kernodle, Alan Leeds, Clyde Brown, Daru Jones, John Curley, R.J. Smith, Otis Williams, Philip Paul and the families of King Records' artists and staff.

About

Yemi Oyediran

Cincinnati filmmaker, jazz drummer and software engineer. King of Them All is his feature debut, nine years in the making, and grew out of a concert series he built around the King catalog. He is a board member of the Percussive Arts Society and Friends of Music Hall.

Afrochine

A Cincinnati media collective founded by Yemi Oyediran and JP Leong. Documentary, music production and education, built around stories that haven't been told yet. afrochine.com

Major funding provided by Greater Cincinnati Foundation, Bailey Lamson Family Foundation, Carol Ann and Ralph V. Haile, Jr. Foundation, Warrington Foundation, and Louise Semple Taft Foundation. Additional funding provided by Ohio Humanities. Presented on PBS through the Open Call for Emerging Filmmakers.
